composition.title: Ares, Aphrodite, Harmonia, Eros, Hephaestus and Poseidon — the whole relation

scenes.title: The song, the bed, and the gods at the door
Bonds beyond the gods' sight
The children belong to their own tellings
The difference that can meet — the bow that is also a lyre
What the apparatus gathers — and where it stalls
The word that takes on the debt
The relation after release

expression:return-of-zero:roz-mytheme-ar.title: Harmonia's line — Cadmus, Ino, Semele, Agave, Autonoë, Polydorus
Harmonia — the form of their countertension
Eros — the desiring between (appointed filial variant)
bow and lyre — the backwards-turning fastening
the goddesses — absent, shame unevenly distributed
Poseidon — the undertaking: he will pay if Ares fails
ἐγγύη — the surety itself, which no apparatus generates
Hephaestus — accepts what he cannot properly refuse; undoes his own work
the loosened bonds — released by the same craft
Thrace — Ares' path out of the song
Paphos — precinct, fragrant altar; the Graces bathe, anoint, clothe
the emptied exhibit — what the bonds achieved, held against what they did not
